cases.purpose: Datagram injection into a live seed: truncated, oversized, malformed, wrong-key, invalid-count and invalid-node datagrams never add members and never prevent a later valid ping; identity conflicts and unsupported types change no roster.
cases.oracle: Independent protocol oracle. Persistent candidate shells run the UNCHANGED builtin as uid 2000 in private state directories on IPv4 loopback inside the disposable VM. The wire format (1212-byte datagram, BCLSTR2 magic, big-endian port, 32-row table, keyed BLAKE2b-256 over the first 1180 bytes) is the fixture's own implementation on hashlib, validated in setup against BLAKE2b known answers and round trips; oracle peers, probes and decoys are owned UDP sockets that validate every request field by field. Expected values never come from candidate output alone: identities and rosters are cross-checked on the wire (authenticated PONG and ROSTER packets), file contents are parsed independently, timing bounds come from the documented deadline (request deadline, heartbeat every quarter, expiry after three), and kernel facts come from /proc (process tree, UDP table, receive queues), inotify, bind() collisions, modes and owners. Setup controls (a failure is an ERROR, never a candidate result): hashing and codec known answers, loopback delivery of 0/1/1212/65507 byte datagrams, the UDP table and its queues, wildcard decoys, every oracle peer mode, inotify atomicity detection, and the persistent-shell driver (status/stdout/stderr extraction, deadline kill, removal of a child that outlives its shell, reaping). Only processes started by the fixture are signaled; every key is evaluated for every vector, an unevaluated key prints ERROR, and any control or fixture exception prints CONTROL-INVALID and exits 97.
cases.comparison: Every key of every vector is evaluated and must be yes. [size-violations] rejected-silently: empty, 1 byte, 8 byte, 600, 1180 and 1211 byte datagrams and 1213, 1312, 2424, 4096 and 65507 byte datagrams produce no reply; roster-unchanged: the members file is byte-identical; later-ping-ok: a later authenticated PING gets a valid PONG; no-queue-drops: the listener receive queue dropped nothing. [format-violations] rejected-silently: signed packets with wrong magic variants and unsigned garbage of the right size produce no reply; roster-unchanged: the members file is byte-identical; later-ping-ok: a later authenticated PING gets a valid PONG; no-queue-drops: the listener receive queue dropped nothing. [mac-violations] rejected-silently: wrong-key, near-key, flipped MAC bits, zero MAC, tampered fields, unkeyed and 64-byte-truncated MACs produce no reply; roster-unchanged: the members file is byte-identical; later-ping-ok: a later authenticated PING gets a valid PONG; no-queue-drops: the listener receive queue dropped nothing. [count-and-node-violations] rejected-silently: signed packets with count 33..255, count 1/5/32 on PING/JOIN/BEAT and node ids that are not 32 lowercase hex digits produce no reply; roster-unchanged: the members file is byte-identical; later-ping-ok: a later authenticated PING gets a valid PONG; no-queue-drops: the listener receive queue dropped nothing. [combined-sequence] all-silent: all four datagram classes in one run produce no reply; roster-unchanged: the roster is unchanged; files-unchanged: the whole state directory snapshot is unchanged; listener-alive: the listener is alive and its receive queue dropped nothing; candidate-ping-ok: the candidate ping to the listener succeeds afterwards; oracle-ping-ok: and so does an authenticated PING. Retained in the case tree: observations.jsonl (every command with its raw stdout, stderr, status and duration, every oracle exchange as hex, teardown findings) and the state directories themselves; the setup report is the stdout of the setup step.
cases.stdout:
size-violations rejected-silently=yes roster-unchanged=yes later-ping-ok=yes no-queue-drops=yes
format-violations rejected-silently=yes roster-unchanged=yes later-ping-ok=yes no-queue-drops=yes
mac-violations rejected-silently=yes roster-unchanged=yes later-ping-ok=yes no-queue-drops=yes
count-and-node-violations rejected-silently=yes roster-unchanged=yes later-ping-ok=yes no-queue-drops=yes
combined-sequence all-silent=yes roster-unchanged=yes files-unchanged=yes listener-alive=yes candidate-ping-ok=yes oracle-ping-ok=yes

cases.purpose: Three-peer roster convergence, leave propagation, heartbeat refresh against silent peer expiry (documented three deadlines), and leaf disconnection after seed loss.
cases.oracle: Independent protocol oracle. Persistent candidate shells run the UNCHANGED builtin as uid 2000 in private state directories on IPv4 loopback inside the disposable VM. cases.comparison: Every key of every vector is evaluated and must be yes. [three-peer-convergence] joins-ok: the seed and two peers started and joined; identities-on-wire: each PONG gives the node id and port, one cluster id, three distinct nodes; rosters-converge: all three members files equal the wire-derived list (seed, peer, peer) within 5 s; members-commands-agree: cluster members prints the same list on each; c-left-status: the third peer leave exits 0; leave-removed-everywhere: the seed and the other peer drop it within 4 s; survivors-intact: both survivors keep their listeners and state=initialized; c-state-cleaned: the leaver state files are gone. [expiry-and-refresh] oracles-joined: two oracle nodes joined the seed next to two candidate peers; silent-expires-not-early: the oracle that never beats leaves the roster no earlier than three deadlines after its join (1.2 s); silent-expires-in-bound: and within three deadlines plus a quarter deadline plus 1.5 s; beating-oracle-retained: the oracle beating every half deadline outlives the silent one by more than two deadlines; beating-peers-retained: the two candidate peers stay in the seed roster at every poll; retention-ends-after-last-beat: the beating oracle expires three deadlines (within the slack) after its last heartbeat; expiry-propagates-to-peers: both candidate peers drop both oracles within 2 s. [seed-loss] peers-joined: seed and leaf joined with equal rosters; seed-left-status: the seed leave exits 0; leaf-disconnected: the leaf state file and status become disconnected within three deadlines plus slack; leaf-roster-self-only: the leaf roster keeps only itself; leaf-listener-alive: the leaf listener is alive; leaf-stopped-after-kill: after SIGKILL of the verified leaf listener, status reports stopped. Retained in the case tree: observations.jsonl (every command with its raw stdout, stderr, status and duration, every oracle exchange as hex, teardown findings) and the state directories themselves; the setup report is the stdout of the setup step.
cases.stdout:
three-peer-convergence joins-ok=yes identities-on-wire=yes rosters-converge=yes members-commands-agree=yes c-left-status=yes leave-removed-everywhere=yes survivors-intact=yes c-state-cleaned=yes
expiry-and-refresh oracles-joined=yes silent-expires-not-early=yes silent-expires-in-bound=yes beating-oracle-retained=yes beating-peers-retained=yes retention-ends-after-last-beat=yes expiry-propagates-to-peers=yes
seed-loss peers-joined=yes seed-left-status=yes leaf-disconnected=yes leaf-roster-self-only=yes leaf-listener-alive=yes leaf-stopped-after-kill=yes
